sampling_query: public desktop browser product with active development; intentionally selected as an event-semantics adversarial review case; previously unseen benchmark repository
frozen_evidence_boundary: repository metadata and pinned git ref
pinned-source code search used only to locate the settings implementation
no issue, PR, discussion, release-history, support or complaint evidence opened before Phase B/C freeze
raw_signal_observation: In the mod-preference checkbox click handler, the code reads whether the XUL checkbox currently has the checked attribute and persists Services.prefs.setBoolPref(key, !checked). The same handler also removes checked when !checked and re-adds checked when checked. Syntactically this looks like a boolean inversion, but the source boundary does not establish whether XUL toggles the checked attribute before the click handler runs.
material_claim: The apparent inversion is below the required mechanism floor until event-order semantics are observed. Editing !checked to checked from static inspection alone could repair a real inversion or introduce one. The cheapest discriminator is a browser-level fixture that observes both visible checked state and persisted pref across a synthesized click.
neta_next_move: Instantiate the checkbox path in a browser-chrome fixture with the preference initially false and true, synthesize one click, and assert both the post-event checked state and persisted preference. Include a deliberate known-wrong assignment as a positive control so the fixture demonstrably turns red.
reversal_condition: If the fixture shows the persisted preference is opposite the visible checkbox state after the event, permit a narrow assignment/handler repair. If event timing makes !checked match the post-click visible state, close the defect claim and leave the code unchanged unless a separate maintainability claim is owner-approved.
baseline_decision: BUILD: the checkbox handler persists the inverse of the checked state; replace Services.prefs.setBoolPref(key, !checked) with checked and simplify the redundant checked-attribute branch.

evidence: Post-freeze exact issue search found no report of mod preference checkboxes persisting the inverse value.
A broader post-freeze issue search returned unrelated tab-unloading and WebRender reports, not evidence for this mechanism.
Post-freeze PR search found no repair or maintainer discussion closing the checkbox event-order question.
adjudication.decision_delta: UNRESOLVED_DELTA: the baseline would change code immediately while Neta requires a browser event fixture. Because no admissible independent evidence resolved XUL event timing, this restraint is not counted as a surviving baseline delta.
adjudication.lesson: Framework event semantics can make an apparent source-level boolean inversion a reviewer trap. Syntax that looks self-contradictory may still sit below the mechanism reality floor when the framework mutates state before the handler observes it.
